title: Store a response apart from its question
statement: Store a completed student or model response as its own evidence record, never inside the question, so it can't leak into the item and blind judging stays possible.
detail: An AP history course's design notes list what every question record holds, the prompt, source set, key or rubric, scoring model, answerability model, provenance and evaluation state, and keep a completed student or model response as a separate evidence record. The stated reason is that this stops a model answer from becoming an accidental part of the question and makes blind evaluation possible. The course's deliverable contract repeats that a response is an evaluation record, not a field of every long-essay or document-based question.

evidence.quote: Every intrinsic question record includes the prompt, source set, key or rubric, scoring model, answerability model, provenance, and evaluation state. A completed student or model response is a separate evidence record. This prevents a model answer from becoming an accidental part of the question and makes blind evaluation possible.
A completed student or model response is an evaluation record, not an intrinsic field of every LEQ or DBQ question.
